risk_if_not_implemented: Without Recovery Operations Criteria, data, software and system images cannot be reliably restored within required recovery objectives following a disruption. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Risk Management Program
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of strategic, operational and tactical risk management controls that are aligned with:
(1) The organization's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM); and
(2) Industry-recognized cybersecurity risk management practices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Risk Management Program (RSK-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Recovery Operations Criteria (BCD-05) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
(1) Routine operations; and
(2) Adverse conditions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) (BCD-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Recovery Operations Criteria (BCD-05) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
